capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists 74.0 kWh usable (itself an estimate) for the 77.4 kWh European IONIQ 6 Long Range (MY23-25), same pack and generation. Compared 2023-2025 (pre-facelift first generation, same E-GMP 77.4 kWh pack/charger; Hyundai US 2023 launch release, EVDB MY23-25 entry, Hyundai US 2024/2025 manuals).

chemistry.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists an NMC cathode for the same 77.4 kWh pack (European MY23-25).

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Hyundai: 800 V architecture; EVDB lists 697 V nominal for the pack. Class read from the 800 V architecture claim (page cites 350 kW charging).

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: navigation trigger (battery heater starts when a charging stop is entered in navigation) from the Hyundai US launch release for the 2023 IONIQ 6; manual control from the CE1 (IONIQ 6) 2024 US owner's manual (src-hyundai-om-ce1-2024-us: Battery Conditioning Mode switch in EV Settings; that page does not itself state that a destination starts the mode and does not name the model). Combined across years, same generation and hardware.
Estimated: companion to the value from src-hyundai-ww-ioniq6-la-2022 (navigation trigger from the 2023 release, manual control from this 2024 CE1 manual page).

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists max DC 233 kW for the European 77.4 kWh IONIQ 6 (MY23-25); Wikipedia infobox also 233 kW. Hyundai itself only states 18 min on a 350 kW charger. Same pack, same generation.

ac_max_kw.notes: US-spec 2023 IONIQ 6 standard 10.9 kW onboard charger (EV Database lists 11 kW for the European car). Applied to the Canadian cars and later years: nothing found that shows a different charger.

published_10_80_min.notes: About 18 minutes from 10 to 80 % on a 350 kW charger at optimal battery temperature (Hyundai US launch release).
